milestone.title: mp surface for post-completion verification.evidence edits

intent.outcome: After this ships, an agent can rewrite `verification.evidence` on a terminal-completion milestone (lifecycle=complete) via `mp milestone update --verification <text>` (and/or `--verification-date` / `--verification-branch` / `--verification-file`). The force_bypass marker (`[force-bypassed:`) is re-evaluated by `evidence_marks_force_bypass()` so clearing the marker in evidence also drops `force_bypassed: true` from `mp show milestone --summary`. Logs record the before/after evidence diff so the post-completion amend shows up in the on-disk milestone file (via `milestone.updated`).

problem.description: After M159 closed with AC-01's ≥30s threshold unmet on real hardware (force-bypassed per F-01 / B-83), the AC's description was rewritten in the 2026-07-13 external review to reflect the actually-measured 17.4s drop via `mp milestone ac bulk`. But the milestone-level `verification.evidence` field still carries the legacy `[force-bypassed: ...]` marker — `mp milestone update --json` rejects the `verification` field with `'verification' — use mp milestone complete --evidence`, and `mp milestone complete` would gate through the full done→complete ceremony and reset `lifecycle`. There is no mp-mediated surface to amend evidence post-completion without losing terminal state. The `evidence_marks_force_bypass()` predicate at `crates/mp/src/milestone_health.rs:127` re-runs on every summary build, so flipping the marker string is sufficient to flip `force_bypassed` — we just need an mp-mediated write path for that field.

in_scope: Extend `mp milestone update` to accept a `--verification` flag (single-line text), `--verification-file <path>` flag (read text from a file; preferred for long evidence), and `--verification-date <YYYY-MM-DD>` + `--verification-branch <name>` companion flags. Mirror the `mp milestone complete --evidence` semantics: the flag only writes if provided; absent flags leave the field alone.

Extend `UpdateMilestoneInput` in `crates/mp/src/milestone/spec.rs:355` to carry an optional `verification: Option<Verification>`. Apply it in `update_milestone` when `Some` (any sub-field None preserves the existing value; the full struct replaces — `cargo test -p mp -E 'test(/milestone.*update/)'` covers the no-op case).
Drop the `'use mp milestone complete --evidence'` error message for `verification` in the unsupported-fields map at `crates/mp/src/milestone/spec.rs:~366` so the new flag is the recommended path.
Stamp `milestone.updated` and (if absent) `verification.date = today()` on every evidence amend so `mp show milestone --summary`'s review_state surfaces a current date.

Verify the `force_bypassed` flag flips: a milestone with `[force-bypassed` in `verification.evidence` reports `force_bypassed: true`; after `mp milestone update --verification "...no force-bypassed..."` it reports `force_bypassed: false`. Add a unit test under `crates/mp/tests/` (or extend `crates/mp/tests/milestone_health.rs` if it exists) covering the flip and the post-completion lifecycle/state preservation.
Document the new flag(s) inline in `mp milestone update --help` and in `docs/concepts/06 - Reference/MP-COMMANDS.md` (update + complete + amend surface).
out_of_scope: Editing post-completion `lifecycle`, `spec_status`, `execution_status`, `findings`, `acceptance_criteria`, or `steps` — those have their own state-machine gates and a future milestone can expose them with similar surfaces if the need reappears.

Audit-trail history of evidence diffs (a tombstone marker like `[amended via mp milestone update at <ts>]` in the new evidence string is the caller's responsibility for now; a future M### can add a per-field history table).
Rewriting M159's existing `verification.evidence` — that lands as the first user of the new surface once M165 ships; M159 block is lifted once the post-completion write is verified end-to-end.

design_decisions.choice: Reuse `mp milestone update --verification` rather than a new `mp milestone amend-evidence` subcommand.
design_decisions.rationale: The existing `UpdateMilestoneInput` already gates per-field writes through `validate_update_milestone_keys`; extending it is ~30 LoC vs ~50 LoC for a new command + new flag. Same write semantics as `mp milestone complete --evidence`, different gate (post-completion allowed). The narrower surface (only `verification`) means we don't accidentally open a path that mutates other post-completion fields — those still need their state-machine transitions.

design_decisions.choice: Caller is responsible for annotating the new evidence with the amend context (e.g., prefix the new evidence string with `[amended via mp milestone update at <ts>; previous evidence cleared]`).
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids a per-field diff log table until a downstream milestone (or M142 L5 audit) needs it. `milestone.updated` already flips; the next reviewer reading `verification.evidence` sees a timestamp + the new narrative. The cost of a structured history table is out of scope.

work_packages.name: Main
work_packages.goal: Add a post-completion evidence-edit surface to mp milestone update; flip force_bypassed when the marker is removed; preserve lifecycle=complete

steps.action: Extend UpdateMilestoneInput in crates/mp/src/milestone/spec.rs to carry verification: Option<Verification> and apply it in update_milestone when Some. UpdateMilestoneInput is a serde-renamed-flatten struct today; add a #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] verification: Option<Verification> field with the same Flatten-friendly shape as the other fields, and in the apply block if let Some(v) = input.verification { m.verification = v; } (sub-fields None preserve existing via serde default). Drop the 'use mp milestone complete --evidence' error message for verification in validate_update_milestone_keys (crates/mp/src/milestone/spec.rs:~366) so the new flag is the recommended path.
steps.done_when: crates/mp/src/milestone/spec.rs UpdateMilestoneInput has verification: Option<Verification> field; update_milestone applies it on Some; the unsupported-fields map no longer lists verification as an error; cargo nextest run on the new evidence-amend tests passes

steps.action: Extend the MilestoneCmd::Update variant in crates/mp/src/cli/milestone.rs with --verification <text>, --verification-file <path>, --verification-date <yyyy-mm-dd>, --verification-branch <name>. Thread them into UpdateMilestoneInput::verification in the cmd_milestone_update handler; absent flags write the None-side of the Optional, preserving existing values via UpdateMilestoneInput's serde defaults. Clamps date format to YYYY-MM-DD; rejects empty --verification silently (use --verification-file instead for long values). Update mp milestone update --help with the four new flags under a new Verification evidence section.
steps.done_when: mp milestone update --help lists --verification, --verification-file, --verification-date, --verification-branch; absent flags leave the existing field alone; --verification-file reads the text from disk

steps.action: Add unit + integration tests: (a) crates/mp/tests/milestone_update_verification.rs — verifies that update_milestone with --verification text persists the new evidence on a lifecycle=complete milestone, leaves lifecycle/spec_status/execution_status unchanged, and updates the modified timestamp; (b) extends evidence_marks_force_bypass unit tests to assert the predicate's behavior is consistent with the predicate's callers (the summary builder). The post-completion amend test creates a fixture milestone via common helpers, marks it complete with a [force-bypassed evidence, then runs mp milestone update --verification 'no marker' and asserts mp show milestone --summary returns force_bypassed=false.
steps.done_when: All new tests pass; lifecycle=complete preserved; force_bypassed flips from true to false after the marker is removed

Add a one-paragraph note about the post-completion amend use case: useful for refreshing the verification.evidence string after a force-bypass was resolved post-completion, or for adding a tombstone marker describing a remediation that landed after the milestone completed.

findings.description: The predicate at crates/mp/src/milestone_health.rs:127 does . During the live M165 smoke, an evidence string that mentions the marker in prose (e.g. 'amended to drop [force-bypassed marker]') still trips the predicate. The fix is to keep the marker literal in evidence when discussing it, or to switch to a tighter regex (e.g. word-boundary anchored). Filed as wontfix for M165 because the substring semantics match the writing path (mp milestone complete --force writes a literal '[force-bypassed:' marker at the start of evidence); the contract is documented in the unit tests and is consistent with the predicate's caller (build_milestone_health_summary). A future tightening could add an M-NNN that requires evidence starts with '[force-bypassed:' or similar — out of M165 scope.
findings.summary: evidence_marks_force_bypass substring match trips on explanatory text
findings.rationale: Discovered while amending M159's evidence during the M165 smoke test: the literal substring '[force-bypassed' inside explanatory prose still trips the predicate. Acceptable for now because callers using --force on mp milestone complete write the canonical '[force-bypassed: ...' marker at the start; only an agent authoring their own evidence (e.g. via M165's new --verification flag) would hit the quirk, and they can phrase the text to avoid the bracket form.

findings.description: The predicate at crates/mp/src/milestone_health.rs:127 does evidence.contains on the marker substring. During the live M165 smoke, an evidence string that mentions the marker in prose (e.g. "amended to drop [force-bypassed marker]") still trips the predicate — the substring appears verbatim. Filed as wontfix for M165 because the substring semantics match the writing path: mp milestone complete --force writes a canonical marker at the start of evidence. The unit tests cover the predicate's contract; callers using --verification via M165's new surface can phrase their text to avoid the bracket form (see live M159 amend where the evidence was rewritten with "the legacy bypass marker has been removed" to flip force_bypassed from true to false). A future tightening could require evidence to start with the canonical marker or use a word-boundary-anchored regex — out of M165 scope.
findings.summary: evidence_marks_force_bypass substring match trips on explanatory text
findings.rationale: Discovered while amending M159's evidence during the M165 smoke test: the literal bracket-form substring inside explanatory prose still trips the predicate. Acceptable for now because callers using --force on mp milestone complete write the canonical marker at the start; only an agent authoring their own evidence via M165's new --verification flag would hit the quirk, and they can phrase the text to avoid the bracket form.

findings.description: crates/mp/src/commands/milestone.rs:419-438 has two empty-value guards: --verification text.is_empty() and --verification_file read_to_string().is_empty(). Both raise anyhow::bail with a structured message. The 4 integration tests in crates/mp/tests/milestone_update_verification.rs (milestone_update_amends_evidence, verifies_unset_field_preserves_value, milestone_update_verification_file_reads_from_disk, milestone_update_verification_date_and_branch_set_companions) all use happy-path evidence strings, so the bails are not covered. Pin them with 2 short tests asserting non-zero exit + stderr contains the expected message.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: Empty --verification / --verification-file guards have no test coverage

findings.description: crates/mp/src/cli/milestone.rs declares --verification-file as Option<PathBuf>; clap accepts an empty value ( followed by empty) which parses to Some(PathBuf::from("")). crates/mp/src/commands/milestone.rs:428 then surfaces fs::read_to_string's std::io error with a 'failed to read --verification-file <empty>' wrapper — the underlying OS error 2 (No such file) maps to 'No such file or directory'. Add an explicit empty-path early bail parallel to the empty-text bail at line 419: if let Some(p) = verification_file { if p.as_os_str().is_empty() { bail!("--verification-file path is empty"); } }.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: Empty --verification-file path errors with low-signal OS message instead of a clear bail

findings.description: crates/mp/src/cli/milestone.rs --verification-branch doc-comment ends with: 'Reachable on lifecycle=complete milestones; mp milestone complete is no longer the only path.' Pre-M165, mp milestone update already worked on any lifecycle — the gating was specifically on the verification field (which UPDATE_MILESTONE_KEYS refused). The 'no longer the only path' framing implies the surface was previously closed, which is misleading. Suggest: 'Reachable on lifecycle=complete milestones; clears the [force-bypassed marker in evidence after a follow-up milestone closes the debt.' Same wording concern applies to --verification and --verification-file doc-comments.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: Doc claim 'mp milestone complete is no longer the only path' reads as if update was previously closed
